anomaly_signals.detail: 136 errors out of 411 spans — 33.1% error rate on payments-service, strongly indicating a payment outage scenario.
50 errors out of 411 spans — 12.2% error rate on the payments database, suggesting DB-layer failures cascading from or causing the payment outage.
193 errors out of 1000 spans — 19.3% error rate, likely reflecting upstream propagation of payment and downstream failures to clients.
35 genai_tool_failures recorded across the batch; tool-executor also shows 26 error spans (5.5% of its 472 spans), indicating degraded tool execution reliability.
26 token truncation events detected on llm-gemini, which also has 24 error spans (2.7% of 875 spans). Truncations may be causing incomplete responses or tool-call failures downstream.
p99 latency of 11,433 ms (>11 seconds) across the batch — far above healthy thresholds, consistent with payment path timeouts and retries propagating through the gateway.

recommended_action: Immediately investigate payments-service and postgres-payments for the root cause of the payment outage (connection exhaustion, query timeouts, or schema issues). Consider circuit-breaking the payment path at the api-gateway to stop cascading client-facing errors. Simultaneously review llm-gemini token truncation config to reduce tool failures, and audit tool-executor error logs for failed tool categories.
summary: A confirmed payment_outage scenario is causing severe degradation: payments-service is failing at a 33% rate and postgres-payments at 12%, together driving a fleet-wide p99 latency of 11.4 seconds and a 5.9% overall error rate. Secondary signals include 35 GenAI tool failures and 26 LLM token truncations, suggesting additional instability in the agent/tool execution layer.
